title: Scaling Latent Reasoning via Looped Language Models
org: ByteDance Seed, with UC Santa Cruz, Princeton, Mila and others
authors: Rui-Jie Zhu, Zixuan Wang, Kai Hua, Tianyu Zhang and 29 others
gist: Open looped models, Ouro, pretrained on 7.7 trillion tokens. A 1.4B or 2.6B stack of layers runs four times per token, and a learned gate can stop early on easy tokens. The authors report the 1.4B roughly matching a 4B dense model and the 2.6B beating an 8B on several reasoning benchmarks, with about a third of the weights.
changes: The strongest case for depth as a lever. When the loop is learned in pretraining, a small model does much of a larger one's job, so weights per unit of quality fall about threefold. Serving pays instead, with four passes per token and a cache for each pass over the prompt.
caveats: Self-reported, against other labs' base models run through the authors' own pipeline, and Qwen3 saw 36 trillion tokens to Ouro's 7.7. The 1.4B trails Qwen3-4B on MMLU, 67.4 against 73.2. Its model card says vLLM always runs all four passes and ignores the early exit, and it pins an older transformers release.
